slides.title: Chat beside the map
slides.html: OpenDefence Matrix puts your OpenDefence chat in a pane under the ATAK map, so you read and write without leaving the map. It is the same chat as the Element X app, so people on either app talk in the same rooms. It opens from the chat button in ATAK's top toolbar, which takes the place of ATAK's own GeoChat. With OpenDefence Main, Chat on its thumb bar at the bottom of the map opens it too once you are signed in.

slides.title: More than text
slides.html: A chat carries photos, videos, files, voice messages and polls as well as text. Photos are sent smaller, to save data.

slides.title: Share from the map
slides.html: You can send a point, route or drawing from the map to a chat, and put what others send on your own map. Each message can also show where it was sent.

slides.title: Kept private
slides.html: Rooms and direct chats made in OpenDefence Matrix are end-to-end encrypted, so only the people in them can read what is said. A message's Message info says so, as here. Photos and videos go without the location stored in the file. Your position goes as the grid under a message, only in encrypted chats, and the pin by the field turns it off.
